Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Isra' (The Night Journey), because it opens with the story of the Isra' from Makkah to al-Quds (Jerusalem). It is a dazzling miracle which Allah singled out for our noble Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as an honour to him, and the account of the Isra' is not mentioned in any other surah.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• Highlighting the miracle of the Isra', as a sign that Allah granted the Prophet ﷺ virtues that He did not grant anyone before him. He was taken by night to Bayt al-Maqdis (the Holy House in Jerusalem), and he led the prophets in prayer there, after it had been abandoned and ruined. This is also an indication that the restoration of al-Masjid al-Aqsa will be carried out by the nation of this Messenger ﷺ, whose message they rejected.

• Discussion of some of the conditions of the Children of Israel in the Holy Land, the corruption they committed, and the punishment that befell them because of it. It also contains a warning to every liar and corrupter, and a threat to the disbelievers of Makkah and to everyone who departs from faith in Allah.

• Discussion of the greatest miracle of the Prophet ﷺ, which is the Noble Qur'an, describing it as guidance, good tidings for those who believe in it, and a warning for those who deny it, and a challenge to both jinn and humankind (al-thaqalan) to produce its like. Within this is the affirmation of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, that the Qur'an is revelation from Allah, and an explanation of its virtue and the virtue of the one to whom it was revealed.

• Showing a number of the virtues and wisdom of the religion of Islam, and teaching Muslims the manners of dealing with Allah, the Exalted, and of dealing with parents and other people who have rights, and good conduct in their behaviour and speech, and being mindful of Allah in their outward and inward conduct.

• Discussion of resurrection and the power to bring it about, and refuting the doubts of the polytheists concerning it with proof and evidence, and warning those who deny by mentioning what befell the nations through the causes of their annihilation and destruction.

• Reminding of the blessings which Allah has subjected to people, and the signs in them of Allah's sole management of creation, and what this requires in terms of thanking the Benefactor and not thanking others, and declaring Him free of any partner and of having children.

• Warning against the incitements of Satan and his enmity toward Adam and his descendants, and his striving to misguide them, and completing this by warning against following Satan and obeying him.

• Mention of the disputation of the polytheists regarding the affirmation of the truthfulness of the Prophet ﷺ; for they were not content with the Qur'an as an everlasting miracle, but instead asked him for material, tangible miracles, which they thought by asking for them would put him to shame and overcome him.

[The Tafsir]

He glorifies Himself and magnifies His status, for His power over what no one else can do; there is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him. He is the One who took His servant Muhammad ﷺ by night for a portion of the night, with his body and spirit, awake and not in a dream, from al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah to al-Masjid al-Aqsa in Bayt al-Maqdis, the area around which Allah blessed with crops, fruits and other things, and He made it a place for many prophets, so that he might witness the wonders of Allah's power and the proofs of His oneness. Indeed Allah, the Exalted, is the All-Hearing of all voices, the All-Seeing of everything seen, and He gives each one what it deserves in this world and the Hereafter.

As God honored Muhammad (ﷺ) with the Night Journey (al-Isra'), so He honored Musa (peace be upon him) by giving him the Torah, making it a clarification of the truth and a guide for the Children of Israel, containing their prohibition from taking anyone other than God as a protector (wali) or as an object of worship to whom they entrust their affairs.

O offspring of those whom We carried with Noah in the Ark! Do not associate anyone with Allah in His worship, and be grateful for His blessings, following the example of Noah, peace be upon him; indeed he was a servant who was greatly thankful to Allah, with his heart, his tongue and his limbs.

This is the commentary on verse 17:4 from al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex). The passage gives the sense of the verse, which concerns the Children of Israel. Here is my translation:

And We informed the Children of Israel, in the Torah that was revealed to them, that they would certainly commit corruption twice in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and its surroundings, through oppression, the killing of the prophets, arrogance, tyranny, and aggression.

So when the first corruption occurs from you, We shall set against you servants of Ours possessing great courage and fierce strength, who will overpower you, kill you, and drive you out of your homes; and they will roam through your homelands spreading corruption. This was a promise that had to come to pass, because its cause existed on your part.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 6:

Then We restored to you, O Children of Israel, the upper hand and victory over your enemies who had been set over you. We increased your wealth and your children, strengthened you, and made you more numerous than your enemy; and that was because of your good conduct and your submission to Allah.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 7:

If you do good in your deeds and your words, you have done good to yourselves, because the reward for that returns to you; and if you do evil, the punishment for that returns upon you. So when the time of the second corruption comes, We will set your enemies over you once again, to humiliate you and overpower you, so that the signs of disgrace and humiliation appear upon your faces, and so that they enter upon you the "Bayt al-Maqdis" (the Holy House, Jerusalem) and destroy it, just as they destroyed it the first time, and so that they utterly annihilate everything that falls under their hands.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 8:

It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you, O Children of Israel, after His punishment. If you repent and amend your conduct, [He will show you mercy]; but if you return to corruption and wrongdoing, We will return to [inflicting] Our punishment and your humiliation. And We have made Hell a prison for you and for the disbelievers in general, from which there is no escape, ever. In this verse and what precedes it, there is a warning to this Ummah against committing sins, lest it be struck by what befell the Children of Israel, for the ways of Allah are one; they are not changed or altered.

This Qur'an, which We have sent down upon Our servant Muhammad (ﷺ), guides people to the most upright of paths, namely the religion of Islam, and gives glad tidings to the believers who act upon what Allah has commanded them and refrain from what He has forbidden them, that for them there is a great reward. And as for those who do not believe in the Last Abode and what it contains of recompense, We have prepared for them a painful punishment in the Fire.

This Qur'an, which We have sent down upon Our servant Muhammad (ﷺ), guides people to the most upright of paths, namely the religion of Islam, and gives glad tidings to the believers who act upon what Allah has commanded them and refrain from what He has forbidden them, that for them there is a great reward. And as for those who do not believe in the Last Abode and what it contains of recompense, We have prepared for them a painful punishment in the Fire.

Man sometimes invokes evil upon himself, his children, or his property in anger, just as he invokes good. This is from the ignorance and hastiness of man. It is also part of God's mercy toward him that He answers his prayers for good and not for evil, because He knows that he does not truly intend that. Man is, by his nature, hasty.

We made the night and the day two signs, indicating Our oneness and Our power. We erased the sign of the night, which is the moon, and made the sign of the day, which is the sun, bright, so that a person may see by the light of day how to conduct the affairs of his livelihood, and may rest and find tranquility in the night. And so that people may know, from the alternation of night and day, the number of years and the reckoning of months and days, and arrange by them whatever they wish of their interests. And We have explained everything with a sufficient explanation.

Every person's deeds, whether good or bad, has God made to cling to him like a collar; he will not be held accountable for another's deeds, nor will another be held accountable for his deeds. On the Day of Resurgence, God will bring forth for him a book in which his deeds have been recorded, and he will find it open before him.

It is said to him: "Read your record," and he reads it, even if he did not know how to read in the world. Your own self is sufficient for you today as a reckoner over you, so that you know what is due to it of recompense. This is among the greatest of justice and fairness: that it be said to the servant, "Take account of yourself; your own self suffices as a reckoner against you."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 15:

Whoever is guided and follows the path of truth, the reward of that returns only to himself, and whoever goes astray and follows the path of falsehood, the punishment for that returns only upon himself. ﴿No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾. And Allah does not punish anyone until the proof has been established against him by the sending of messengers and the sending down of books.

When We intend to destroy a town for its wrongdoing, We command its affluent ones to obey Allah, to worship Him alone, and to believe in His messengers. The others are followers of them. But they disobeyed the command of their Lord and denied His messengers, so the word of punishment, which cannot be averted, was justified against them, and We utterly annihilated them.

And how many generations have We destroyed after Noah, [generations] that denied their messengers. And your Lord, O Messenger, is sufficient as one who is All-Aware of the deeds of His servants; nothing about them is hidden from Him.

Whoever desires the hasty life of this world, and strives for it alone, not believing in the Hereafter nor working for it, Allah hastens for him therein whatever He wills and intends for whom He wishes, of what He has decreed for him in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). Then We make Hell his destination in the Hereafter, to enter it blameworthy and expelled from the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. That is because of his desire for this world and his striving for it, to the exclusion of the Hereafter.

Whoever intends by his good deed the reward of the Hereafter, the everlasting abode, and strives for it through obedience to Allah, while he is a believer in Allah, His reward, and His great recompense, then those people's deed is accepted and stored up for them with their Lord, and they will be rewarded for it.

Each group, of those who work for the perishable world and of those who work for the everlasting Hereafter, We increase from Our provision. So We provide for both the believers and the disbelievers in this world, for provision is a bounty from your Lord, granted out of His grace, and the bounty of your Lord is never withheld from anyone, whether believer or disbeliever.
Reflect, O Messenger, on how God has favored some people over others in this world, in provision and in works. Yet the Hereafter holds greater degrees for the believers, and greater favor.
Do not make, O human being, any partner with Allah in worship, lest you incur blame and abandonment.

And your Lord has decreed, commanded and made obligatory that you, O human being, worship none but Him alone, the Glorified and Exalted. And He has commanded you to show kindness to your father and mother, especially when they reach old age and are in your care. So do not be impatient with them or find burdensome anything you see from either of them or both, and do not let them hear any harsh word, not even "uff" (ta'fif, an expression of annoyance), which is the lowest degree of harsh speech. Nor should any ugly deed proceed from you toward them. Rather, be gentle with them, and always speak to them with soft, kind words.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 24:

Be humble and gentle toward your mother and father, out of mercy for them, and ask your Lord to have mercy on them with His vast mercy, both while they are alive and after they die, just as they endured hardship in raising you when you were a child, weak and powerless.

Your Lord knows best what is in your hearts, of good and of evil. If your intention and aim is to seek the pleasure of God and what brings you closer to Him, then indeed He is, glory be to Him, ever Forgiving to those who turn back to Him at all times. Whoever God knows has in his heart nothing but turning back to Him and love for Him, He will pardon him and forgive him whatever minor sins occur to him, those that arise from the nature of human beings.

"Show kindness to every relative who has a claim of kinship upon you, and give him his right of kindness and goodness. Give to the needy person who does not possess what suffices him and meets his need, and to the traveler cut off from his family and wealth. Do not spend your wealth in other than obedience to Allah, or in a manner of extravagance and squandering."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 27:

Indeed, those who squander (al-musrifin) and those who spend their wealth in acts of disobedience to Allah are the likes of the devils in evil, corruption and disobedience. And Satan was greatly ungrateful and intensely denying of the blessing of his Lord.

And if you turn away from them, awaiting a mercy from your Lord that you hope for, [in order to avoid giving to those you were commanded to give to, due to not having anything to give them], then speak to them a gentle, kind word, such as praying for them to be made wealthy and given abundant provision, and promise them that when God grants you provision from His bounty, you will give them from it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 29:

Do not keep your hand tied (stingy) from spending in the cause of good, constricting yourself, your family, and the needy; and do not be extravagant in spending, so that you give beyond your means, and thus sit condemned, blamed by people who reproach and censure you, regretful over your squandering and the loss of your wealth.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 30:

Indeed, your Lord expands provision for whom He wills among the people and restricts it for others, according to His knowledge and wisdom, glory be to Him and exalted is He. Indeed, He is the One who is fully aware of the hidden matters of His servants; nothing of their circumstances escapes His knowledge.

The commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 31:

And when you know that provision is in the hand of Allah, the Exalted, then do not kill your children, O people, for fear of poverty. For He, the Exalted, is the Provider of His servants; He provides for the children as He provides for the parents. Indeed, killing children is a great sin.
Do not draw near to adultery or the things that lead to it, so that you do not fall into it. Indeed, it was an act of extreme ugliness, and evil is the path that it represents.

Do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden to be killed, except by the legal right, such as retaliation (qisas), stoning the adulterer who is married (muhsan), or killing the apostate. Whoever is killed unjustly, We have given his heir (wali) — whether an heir or a ruler — a claim (hujjah) to demand the killing of his killer or the blood money (diyah). But it is not permissible for the guardian of the one who was killed to exceed the limit of Allah in retaliation, such as killing two for one or a group, or mutilating the killer. Indeed, Allah helps the guardian of the one who was killed against the killer, so that he may be enabled to kill him in retribution (qisas).

This is a tafsir passage (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, from the King Fahd Complex commentary), so I'll translate it as it stands.

And do not dispose of the property of orphaned children whose fathers have died while they are still below the age of maturity and have come under your guardianship, except in the way that is best for them, which is to invest and grow it, until the orphan child reaches the age of maturity and sound judgment in managing wealth. And fulfil every covenant you have made. Indeed, the covenant will be questioned about by Allah on the Day of Resurrection concerning its one who made it, so He will reward him if he fulfilled and honoured it, and punish him if he betrayed it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 35:

Give full measure when you measure out, and do not diminish it when you measure for others. Weigh with a balanced scale. Justice in measuring and weighing is better for you in this world, and its outcome is finer with Allah in the Hereafter.

Do not follow, O human, that of which you have no knowledge; rather, verify and make certain. Indeed, the human being will be held accountable for what he employed his hearing, his sight, and his heart for. So if he employs them for good, he will attain reward, and if he employs them for evil, he will attain punishment.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 37:

Do not walk on the earth arrogantly and boastfully; for you will never tear the earth apart by your walking upon it in this manner, nor will you ever reach the mountains in height by your conceit, pride and haughtiness.
All that has been mentioned above of commands and prohibitions: Allah dislikes its evil, and He does not approve of it for His servants.

That which We have explained and clarified of these noble rulings, from the commands to good deeds and the prohibitions of base morals, is among what We have revealed to you, O Prophet. And do not make, O human being, another deity alongside Allah in His worship, lest you be cast into the Fire of Hell, blamed by yourself and by the people, and become one who is cast out and distanced from every good.

Will your Lord, O polytheists, have favored you with sons, and taken for Himself daughters from the angels? Indeed, you are saying a monstrous and grievous utterance; it is not befitting to Allah, glory be to Him and exalted.

We have indeed clarified and varied in this Qur'an the rulings, the parables, and the admonitions, so that people may take heed, reflect on what benefits them so that they adopt it, and on what harms them so that they abandon it. Yet this clarification and explanation only increases the wrongdoers in their distance from the truth and in their heedlessness of contemplation and taking lessons.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 42:

Say, O Messenger, to the polytheists: If there were other gods with Allah, as you claim, then those gods would have sought a way to overpower Allah, the Lord of the Mighty Throne.
Glorified is Allah and exalted above what the polytheists say; He is far exalted above it, with a great exaltation.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 44:

The seven heavens and the earth, and whoever is in them of all creatures, glorify Him, exalted is He. Everything in this existence glorifies God, exalted is He, with a glorification joined with praise and commendation to Him, glory be to Him. But you, O people, do not comprehend that glorification. Indeed, He, glory be to Him, is ever Forbearing toward His servants, not hastening to punish those who disobey Him, and Forgiving toward them.

When you recite the Qur'an and these polytheists hear it, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a concealing veil that blocks their minds from understanding the Qur'an, as a punishment for their disbelief and their denial.

We have placed coverings over the hearts of the polytheists so that they do not understand the Qur'an, and We have placed deafness in their ears so that they do not hear it. And when you mention your Lord in the Qur'an, calling to His tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness) and forbidding association with Him (shirk), they turn back on their heels, fleeing from your words, out of arrogance and out of pride at the idea that they should single out God, exalted is He, in worship.

We know best why the leaders of Quraysh listen, when they listen to you while their intentions are evil. Their listening is not for the sake of seeking guidance or accepting the truth. We also know their secret conferring when they say: "You are only following a man who has been affected by sorcery and whose mind has become confused."
Reflect, O Messenger, in wonder at their saying: "Muhammad is a sorcerer, a poet, a madman!!" They have strayed and deviated, and have not been guided to the path of truth and rightness.
And the polytheists said, denying that they could be created anew after their bones have decayed and become crumbled dust: "Will we really be raised up on the Day of Resurrection in a new creation?"

Say to them, O Messenger, as a challenge: "Be stones or iron in hardness and strength, if you are able to do so. Or be a creation even greater, one that seems far-fetched to your minds to accept." Then they will say, denying: "Who will return us to life after death?" Say to them: "The One who will bring you back and restore you is Allah, who originated you from nothingness the first time." When they hear this reply, they will shake their heads, mocking and astonished, and they will say, deeming it far-fetched: "When will this resurrection take place?" Say: "What would make you know that this resurrection, which you deny and consider far-fetched, may be near at hand?"

Say to them, O Messenger, as a challenge: "Be stones or iron in hardness and strength, if you are able to do so. Or be a creation even greater, one that seems far-fetched to your minds to accept." Then they will say, denying: "Who will return us to life after death?" Say to them: "The One who will bring you back and restore you is Allah, who originated you from nothingness the first time." When they hear this reply, they will shake their heads, mocking and astonished, and they will say, deeming it far-fetched: "When will this resurrection take place?" Say: "What would make you know that this resurrection, which you deny and consider far-fetched, may be near at hand?"

On the Day when your Creator calls you forth from your graves, you will respond to the command of God, submitting to Him, and all praise belongs to Him in every state. And, because of the terror of the Day of Resurrection, you will think that you remained in the world only a little while, owing to the length of your stay in the Hereafter.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 17, verse 53:

And say to My servants, the believers, that they should speak in their address and discourse with the best and kindest words; for if they do not do so, Satan will sow enmity, corruption and quarrel among them. Indeed, Satan has ever been to man a manifest enemy.

Your Lord knows you best, O people. If He wills, He will have mercy on you and guide you to faith; or if He wills, He will let you die in disbelief and punish you. We have not sent you, O Messenger, to be a guardian over them, managing their affairs and recompensing them for their deeds. Your only duty is to convey what you were sent with and to make clear the straight path.

Your Lord, O Messenger, knows best who is in the heavens and the earth. And We have favored some of the prophets over others with virtues, the number of their followers, and the revelation of scriptures, and We gave David (peace be upon him) the Psalms (al-Zabur).

Say, O Messenger, to the polytheists among your people: "Those whom you call upon, to remove harm from you, do not possess that power, nor are they able to transfer it from you to anyone else, nor are they able to change it from one state to another. The One able to do that is Allah alone." This verse is general in its meaning, applying to everything that is called upon besides Allah, whether dead or absent, whether prophets, righteous people, or others, and whether by the words of seeking relief (istighathah), supplication (du'a), or anything else. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.

This is the commentary on verse 57 of Surah al-Isra' (17), from the Tafsir al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex):

Those whom the polytheists call upon, such as the prophets, the righteous, and the angels, besides Allah, are themselves competing to draw near to their Lord by whatever good deeds they are able to perform. They hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is something that the servants should beware of and fear.

God threatens the disbelievers that there is no disbelieving town that denies the messengers except that He will send down upon it His punishment, by destruction in this world before the Day of Resurrection, or by severe torment for its people. This is a decree that Allah has written and a judgment He has settled, which must certainly come to pass, and it is inscribed in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

The commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 59:

And nothing prevented Us from sending the miracles that the polytheists asked for except that the earlier nations denied them. For God granted them what they requested, but they denied and were destroyed. And We gave Thamud, the people of Salih, a clear miracle, namely the she-camel, but they disbelieved in it, so We destroyed them. And Our sending of the messengers with the signs, lessons and miracles that We placed in their hands was only a warning to the servants, so that they might take heed and be mindful.

Remember, O Messenger, when We told you: "Indeed, your Lord encompasses mankind in knowledge and power." And We did not make the vision which We showed you with your own eyes on the night of the Isra' and Mi'raj (the Night Journey and Ascension) a wonder of creation, except as a trial for people, so that the disbelievers among them might be distinguished from the believers. And We did not make the cursed tree of zaqqum (the tree of Hell) which is mentioned in the Qur'an except as a trial for people. We warn the polytheists with various kinds of punishment and signs, but the warning only increases them in transgression and misguidance.

Remember when We said to the angels: "Prostrate to Adam," as a greeting and an honouring. So they all prostrated, except Iblis (Iblis). He became arrogant and refused to prostrate, saying in denial and arrogance: "Shall I prostrate to one whom You have made from clay, this weak creature?"

Iblis said, in audacity against Allah and disbelief in Him: "Have You seen this creature whom You have honored over me? If You grant me respite until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely take control over his descendants through misleading and corruption, except for those among them who are sincere in faith, and they are few."

God Most High said, threatening Iblis and his followers: "Go, and whoever among the descendants of Adam follows you and obeys you, indeed your punishment and theirs is a full and complete recompense in the Fire of Hell."

Tafsir (Qur'anic commentary) of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 64:

And incite to rebellion whomever you can among them with your call to them to disobey Me, and gather against them every force you are able to muster of your cavalry and infantry, and make for yourself a share in their wealth by their earning it through what is unlawful and spending it on that, and a share in their children through adorning fornication and sins for them and opposing the commands of Allah, until immorality and corruption become widespread, and promise your followers from the descendants of Adam false promises, for all of Satan's promises are vain and deception.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 65:

Indeed, My sincere believing servants who obeyed Me, you (Satan) have no power to lead them astray. And your Lord, O Prophet, is sufficient as a protector and guardian for the believers against the schemes and deceit of Satan.

Your Lord, O people, is the One who makes the ships run for you across the sea, so that you may seek the bounty of Allah in your travels and trade. Indeed, Allah has always been Most Merciful to His servants.

When distress befalls you at sea, those you invoke other than Him vanish from your minds, and you turn to God alone to rescue and deliver you. But when He brings you safely to land, you turn away. Man is ever ungrateful.

Have you then become heedless, O people, of the punishment of God, so that you feel secure that He will not cause the earth to swallow you up, or send against you a storm of stones from the sky that destroys you, and then you will find no one to protect you from His punishment?

Or do you feel secure, O people, that your Lord will not send you back to the sea another time and unleash upon you a violent wind that shatters everything it strikes, so that He drowns you for your disbelief, and then you will find no one to pursue you on our account or to make a claim against us? For indeed Allah has not wronged you even by the weight of an atom.

We have honored the children of Adam with reason and the sending of messengers. We have subjected to them everything in the universe, subjected to them the beasts on land and the ships at sea to carry them, provided them with good and wholesome food and drink, and favored them over many of the creatures with a great favor.

Remember, O Messenger, the Day of Resurrection, when you will bring glad tidings and give warning: the day when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, calls every community of people together with their leader whom they used to follow in the world. Whoever among them was righteous and is given his record of deeds in his right hand, these will read the record of their good deeds joyfully and rejoicing, and they will not be wronged of the reward of their righteous deeds in the least, even by the amount of the thread that is in the slit of a date-stone.

Whoever is blind of heart in this world, unable to see the signs of Allah's power, and does not believe in what the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) brought, will be even more blind on the Day of Resurrection, in finding the path to Paradise, and even further astray from guidance and right direction.

The Mushrikun almost tempted you, O Messenger, to turn away from the Qur'an that Allah has revealed to you, so that you would invent something other than what We revealed to you. Had you done what they wanted, they would have taken you as a close friend.

Had We not made you firm (upon the truth) and preserved you from agreeing with them, you would nearly have inclined towards them somewhat in what they proposed to you, owing to the strength of their deception and the severity of their scheming, and owing to your eagerness for their guidance.

This is the commentary on Surah 17 (al-Isra'), verse 75, from the Tafsir al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex):

"And had We not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined toward them a little." Here the commentary explains the verse's meaning: O Messenger, had you inclined toward these polytheists even slightly in what they asked of you, We would have made you taste double the punishment of life in this world and double the punishment of death in the Hereafter. That would be because of the completeness of Allah's favor upon you and the perfection of your knowledge of your Lord. Then you would not find anyone to help you or to ward off Our punishment from you.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 76:

The disbelievers came close to driving you out of Makkah by their harassment of you. Had they done so, they would not have remained in it after you except for a short time, until the immediate punishment befell them.
That is the way of Allah, the Exalted, in destroying a nation that expels its Messenger from among them. And you will not find, O Messenger, any change in Our way; there is no failing in Our promise.

Establish the prayer in its completeness from the decline of the sun at midday until the darkness of the night, which includes the Dhuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib and 'Isha prayers. And establish the Fajr prayer, and lengthen the recitation in it; for the Fajr prayer is attended by the angels of the night and the angels of the day.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 79:

Rise, O Prophet, from your sleep for part of the night and recite the Qur'an in the prayer of the night. Let the night prayer be an addition for you, raising your rank and elevating your degrees, so that perhaps Allah will raise you up as one who intercedes for the people on the Day of Resurrection, that Allah may have mercy on them from what they will be in, and you will be placed in a station for which you will be praised by the first and the last.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, a concise *tafsir*, or Qur'anic exegesis) on Surah 17, verse 80:**

﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance, and cause me to exit a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority."﴾

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 81:

Say, O Messenger, to the polytheists: Islam has come and polytheism has departed. Falsehood has no permanence and no stability, while the truth is what endures and abides, which does not vanish.

We send down from the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy to the believers, [and] the wrongdoers it increases in nothing but loss.

Wait, I should translate only the passage given. Here is the faithful translation:

We send down of the verses of the Mighty Qur'an that which heals the hearts from diseases such as doubt, hypocrisy and ignorance, and that which heals the bodies through its recitation as a remedy (ruqyah), and that which is a means of attaining the mercy of God through what it contains of faith. And this Qur'an does not increase the disbelievers, upon hearing it, in anything but disbelief and misguidance, because of their denial of it and their failure to believe in it.

When We bestow favour upon man, with wealth, good health, or the like, he turns away and distances himself from obedience to his Lord; and when hardship befalls him, such as poverty or illness, he becomes despairing, because he does not trust in the bounty of Allah, the Exalted, except those whom Allah has protected in both their times of ease and their times of adversity.
Say, [O Messenger], to the people: Each one of you acts according to his own disposition and condition, and your Lord knows best who is most rightly guided in the way.

The disbelievers ask you about the reality of the soul, out of obstinacy. So answer them: the reality of the soul and its states are among the matters that God has kept to Himself in knowledge, and you have been given, you and all people, only a little knowledge.

And if We willed, We could take away what We have revealed to you (of the Qur'an); then you would find no one to plead your cause against Us in that matter, nor anyone to restore it to you.

Note: The Qur'anic verse quoted here is ﴿وَلَئِن شِئْنَا لَنَذْهَبَنَّ بِالَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ﴾ — hmm, that is not the exact text of this passage; the passage above is the translation of the commentary as it stands.

But Allah has shown you mercy, so affirm that in your heart. Indeed, His bounty upon you has been great. He has given you this magnificent Qur'an and the praiseworthy station, and other things He has not given to anyone else among the worlds.
Say: "If mankind and the jinn were to gather together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would never be able to produce its like, even if they helped one another and backed each other up."

This is a tafsir passage on Q 17:89, so the verse itself should be rendered in ﴿ ﴾ markers. The passage paraphrases the verse rather than quoting it directly, so I translate the commentary text as it stands.

And We have certainly explained and varied for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example worthy of being taken as a lesson, establishing proof against them thereby, so that they would follow it and act upon it. Yet most people refused except to deny the truth and reject the proofs and evidences of Allah.

When the Qur'an had left the polytheists powerless and overcome them, they began demanding miracles that suited their whims, saying: "We will not believe you, O Muhammad, nor act upon what you say, until you cause a flowing spring to gush forth for us from the earth of Makkah."
Or you have a garden of date palms and grapevines, and you make rivers flow abundantly through its midst.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 92:

Or cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed, or bring Allah and His angels before us, so that we may see them face to face and directly.

Or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascent until you bring down to us a book that we may read." Say, [O Messenger], in wonder at the obstinacy of these disbelievers: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?" (Subhan Rabbi: "Glory be to my Lord!")

Note: The translation above reproduces the Quranic verse as rendered in the translator's source, while the commentary portion follows below.

Translation of the commentary:

Or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky (fi as-sama', "into the sky"). And we will not believe in your ascent until you come down to us with a book from Allah, spread open, which we read and in which we find that you are truly the Messenger of Allah. Say, O Messenger, expressing amazement at the obstinacy of these disbelievers: "Glory be to my Lord (Subhan Rabbi, a phrase of glorification and exclamation of wonder)! Am I anything but a human being, one of His servants, who conveys His message? So how could I be able to do what you demand?"

Nothing prevented the disbelievers from believing in God and His Messenger and obeying them, once the clear proof had come to them from God, except their saying, out of ignorance and denial: "Has God sent a messenger from among mankind?"

Say, [O Messenger], in reply to the polytheists who denied that a messenger could be a human being: "If there were angels walking peacefully upon the earth, We would have sent down to them a messenger from among their own kind. But the people of the earth are human beings, so the messenger sent to them must be of their own kind, so that they can address him and understand his speech."

Say, "Allah suffices as a witness between me and you to attest to my truthfulness and the reality of my prophethood. Indeed, He is All-Aware of the conditions of His servants and All-Seeing of their deeds, and He will recompense them for them."

Whoever Allah guides is the one truly guided to the truth, and whoever Allah leaves to stray, forsaking him and leaving him to himself, for him there is no guide besides Allah. These misguided ones, Allah will raise them on the Day of Resurrection and gather them upon their faces, blind, mute and deaf. Their destination is the Fire of Hell, blazing. Whenever its flame subsides and its fire dies down, We increase them in fire, blazing and flaring.

This punishment that has been described is the requital for the polytheists, because of their disbelief in the signs and proofs of Allah, their denial of His messengers who called them to worship Him, and their saying, in denial, when they were commanded to affirm the Resurrection: "When we have died and become bones decayed and fragments crumbled, will we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?"

Have these polytheists become heedless, so that they do not reflect and realize that God, who created the heavens and the earth and what is in them of creatures without any prior model, is able to create their likes after their annihilation? God has appointed for these polytheists a specific time for their death and their punishment, about which there is no doubt that it will come upon them. Yet despite the clarity of the truth and its proofs, the disbelievers have refused except to deny the religion of God, Mighty and Majestic.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: "If you possessed the treasuries of my Lord's mercy, which never run out and never perish, then you would surely withhold them, and would not give any of them to others, fearing that they would be depleted and you would become poor. It is the nature of man to be stingy with what is in his hand, except for those whom God protects with faith."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 101:

We gave Musa nine clear miracles, which were evident signs of the truthfulness of his prophethood. They were: the staff, the hand, the years of drought, the loss of fruits, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood. So ask the Children of Israel, O Messenger, as a question seeking confirmation, about the time when Musa came to their forefathers with his clear miracles. Pharaoh said to Musa: "Indeed, I think you, O Musa, are a sorcerer, deluded and with your mind overcome by the strange deeds you bring."

Moses replied to him: "You have certainly known, O Pharaoh, that none sent down these nine clear signs, which bear witness to the truth of my prophethood, except the Lord of the heavens and the earth, as evidence by which those of insight might recognize God's oneness in His lordship and His divinity. And indeed, I am certain, O Pharaoh, that you are doomed, cursed, and defeated."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 103:

Pharaoh intended to drive Moses out and expel him, together with the Children of Israel, from the land of "Egypt," so We drowned him and those with him of his soldiers in the sea, as a punishment for them.

And We said, after the destruction of Pharaoh and his army, to the Children of Israel: "Dwell in the land" of "al-Sham" (Greater Syria), "and when the Hereafter comes, We will bring you all forth from your graves to the place of reckoning."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 105:

And with truth We sent down this Qur'an upon Muhammad (ﷺ), to command the servants and forbid them, and (to announce) their reward and their punishment; and with truthfulness, justice, and preservation from alteration and substitution did it descend. And We did not send you, O Messenger, except as a bringer of good tidings of Paradise to whoever obeys, and a warner of the Fire to whoever disobeys and disbelieves.

And We have sent down to you, O Messenger, a Qur'an which We have made clear, firmly established, and explained in detail, distinguishing between guidance and misguidance, and truth and falsehood; so that you may recite it to the people slowly and deliberately. And We have sent it down in parts, piece by piece, according to events and the requirements of circumstances.

Say, O Messenger, to these deniers: "Believe in the Qur'an or do not believe. Your belief does not add to its perfection, and your denial does not diminish it. Indeed, those of knowledge who were given the earlier scriptures before the Qur'an, and who recognized the reality of revelation, when it is recited to them, fall down in prostration upon their faces, out of glorification of Allah, the Exalted, and gratitude to Him."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 17, verse 108:

And those who were given knowledge say, upon hearing the Qur'an: "Glory be to our Lord, and exalted is He above what the polytheists ascribe to Him. The promise of Allah, of reward and punishment, is nothing but something that will certainly come to pass."

These [people] fall down in prostration on their faces, weeping, moved by the admonitions of the Qur'an. And hearing the Qur'an and its admonitions increases them in humility before the command of Allah and His great power.

Say, O Messenger, to the polytheists of your people who objected to your invoking God by saying "O Allah, O Merciful": call upon Allah, or call upon the Merciful. Whichever of His names you call upon, [know that] you are calling upon one Lord, for all His names are the most beautiful. And do not recite aloud in your prayer, so that the polytheists hear you, nor recite in a low voice, so that your companions do not hear you; and seek a middle course between loudness and whispering.

And say, [O Messenger]: "All praise is due to Allah, to whom belongs perfection and commendation, who is exalted above having a son or a partner in His divinity, and who has no protector (walī) among His creation, for He is the Self-Sufficient, the Mighty, while they are the poor who are in need of Him. Glorify Him with complete glorification, by praising Him, worshipping Him alone with no partner, and making the religion entirely sincere to Him."
